title: The efficacy of radical antegrade modular pancreatosplenectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol
author: Jun Watanabe
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bxhfpj3n

steps.title: Define Study Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria
steps.instruction: Establish the parameters for selecting articles and participants for the systematic review.

substeps.instruction: Include randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-RCTs comparing RAMPS with SRPS, regardless of language, country, publication year, or observation period.
Include published articles, unpublished articles, conference abstracts, and letters; exclude reviews, letters, and case reports.
Include adult patients (aged >18 years) scheduled for pancreatectomy with pancreatic malignancy.
Exclude patients who did not provide consent.

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Execute a comprehensive search across electronic databases and other resources to identify relevant studies.

substeps.instruction: Search MEDLINE (PubMed), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (Cochrane Library), and EMBASE (Dialog) using the specific search strategies detailed in Appendix 1.
Search the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP) and ClinicalTrials.gov for ongoing or unpublished trials.
Review reference lists of eligible studies, articles citing eligible studies, and international guidelines.
Contact original authors for unpublished or additional data.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Filter identified articles to determine eligibility through a multi-reviewer process.

substeps.instruction: Two independent reviewers (JW and KR) screen titles and abstracts.
Assess eligibility based on full texts.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or by a third reviewer (KK) acting as an arbiter.
Contact original authors if relevant data is missing.

steps.title: Extract and Manage Data
steps.instruction: Systematically collect data from included studies using a standardized approach.

substeps.instruction: Two reviewers (JW and KR) perform independent data extraction using a standardized collection form.
Validate the form using 10 randomly selected studies.
Extract information on study design, study population, interventions, and outcomes.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or by a third reviewer (KK) acting as an arbiter.

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality and bias of the included studies.

substeps.instruction: Two reviewers (JW and KR) independently evaluate risk of bias using Risk of Bias 2 or the Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Rating Scale.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or by a third reviewer (KR) acting as an arbiter.

steps.title: Analyze Treatment Effects
steps.instruction: Pool data and calculate effect sizes for primary and secondary outcomes.

substeps.instruction: Pool relative risk ratios and 95% CIs for binary variables: postoperative complications, POPF, and R0 resection.
Pool mean differences and 95% CIs for continuous variables: harvested lymph nodes, blood loss, and operative time (use standard mean differences (SMDs) if scales vary).
Pool hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs for primary outcomes: OS, RFS, and DFS.

steps.title: Address Unit of Analysis and Missing Data
steps.instruction: Apply statistical corrections for cluster-RCTs and handle missing information.

substeps.instruction: For cluster-RCTs with dichotomous data, apply the design effect and calculate effective sample size/events using the intra-cluster correlation coefficient (ICC) or a substitute from a similar study.
For cluster-RCTs with continuous data, reduce the sample size while keeping means and standard deviation unchanged.
Request missing data from original authors.
Perform intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis for dichotomous data; do not impute missing continuous data.
Calculate missing standard deviations using the Altman method or via confidence interval and t-value based on Cochrane handbook/validated methods.

steps.title: Evaluate Heterogeneity and Reporting Bias
steps.instruction: Assess the consistency of results and the potential for publication bias.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate statistical heterogeneity via forest plots and the I2 statistic (0-40%: not important; 30-60%: moderate; 50-90%: substantial; 75-100%: considerable).
Investigate reasons for heterogeneity if I2 > 50%.
Compare outcomes defined in trial protocols with reported outcomes using ClinicalTrials.gov and ICTRP.
Assess publication bias via visual inspection of funnel plots (only if 10 or more trials are found).

steps.title: Perform Meta-Analysis and Subgroup/Sensitivity Analysis
steps.instruction: Synthesize data using software and test the robustness of the results.

substeps.instruction: Perform meta-analysis using Review Manager software (RevMan 5.4.2) with a random-effects model.
Conduct subgroup analysis for primary outcomes based on country (Asia vs. Western countries) if data is sufficient.
Perform sensitivity analyses by: excluding studies with imputed statistics, including only patients with complete data, and including only patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

steps.title: Generate Summary of Findings
steps.instruction: Determine the certainty of evidence and summarize the results.

substeps.instruction: Two reviewers (JW and KR) evaluate evidence certainty using the GRADE approach, with KK as arbiter.
Create a summary of findings table for OS, RFS, DFS, R0 resection, harvested lymph nodes, and postoperative complications based on the Cochrane handbook.
